summary: The note surveys community-led mental health awareness initiatives launched since September 2023, aimed at reducing stigma and encouraging people to seek help. Programs span a festival, school education, culturally sensitive services for marginalized groups, a mobile app, workplace wellness, peer support networks, and arts-based therapy. Together they show a movement turning awareness into practical, accessible support.
one_line: Overview of community initiatives since September 2023 that raise mental health awareness through festivals, schools, apps, workplaces, peer support and arts.
key_facts: Jackson Heights hosted the inaugural "Mind Matters" festival in October under Emily Torres' direction with volunteers, featuring workshops, keynote addresses and testimonials; it is expected to become annual.

Beginning September 2023, a coalition led by Dr. Angela Roberts began the "Healthy Minds in Schools" initiative, adding age-appropriate mental health education to schools in the Austin Independent School District.
"Healthy Minds in Schools" teaches students to manage stress, empathize with others and recognize signs of mental illness, aiming to normalize conversations about mental health.
"Cultural Compass" launched in December 2023 under social worker Michael Liu, targeting minorities, LGBTQ+ individuals and people living in poverty who face barriers to mental healthcare.
"Cultural Compass" is a network of providers offering culturally sensitive counseling and support groups, plus multilingual mental health navigators who help people move through healthcare systems.
Tech entrepreneur Priya Singh released the app "Mental Health Mate" in January 2024, with emergency chat staffed by trained volunteers, mood tracking and a directory of local mental health resources.
"Mental Health Mate" has had thousands of monthly active users since its debut and lets users connect anonymously with others facing similar challenges.

"Operation Mindful Workspace" was launched in February 2024 by HR expert Jonathan Clark to train managers in mental health first aid, give employees mental health days off and create meditation and relaxation spaces.
"Operation Mindful Workspace" has drawn interest from companies across the country, with benefits including improved well-being, higher productivity and reduced absenteeism.
Mental health counselor Susan O'Connell founded the "Together We Thrive" peer support network in May 2024 to provide regular meetups and train peer support facilitators.
"Together We Thrive" has expanded quickly into communities nationwide, with peer groups acting as gateways to other mental health services.
Local artist and therapist Laura Zhang launched "Art of Wellness" in March 2024, offering workshops in art therapy, dance, music and drama for mental wellbeing.
